claim: State-enforced racial segregation in public schools violates the Equal Protection Clause.
Before custodial interrogation, police must warn a suspect about the right to remain silent and the right to counsel.
An indigent criminal defendant charged with a felony has a right to appointed counsel in state court.
Evidence obtained through an unconstitutional search or seizure is inadmissible in a state criminal prosecution.
Public-school students retain First Amendment speech rights unless officials can reasonably forecast substantial disruption.
Advocacy may be punished only when it is directed to inciting imminent lawless action and is likely to produce it.
A public official suing over statements about official conduct must prove actual malice.
case_name: New York Times Co. v. Sullivan
